extracted.intended_audience: researchers, grant program administrators, and policymakers interested in the peer review of grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing and improving the peer-review process for grant applications, focusing on reliability, validity, bias, generalizability, assessor selection, and alternative review systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional psychological research criterion: whether peer reviews produce consistent, dependable ratings across assessors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors report that peer reviews 'lacked reliability.' Reliability should be empirically evaluated (e.g., inter-rater consistency); improving reliability was a central motivation for proposing alternative systems like the reader system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional psychological research criterion: whether peer-review ratings accurately reflect the quality or merit they purport to measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validity must be assessed alongside reliability; the paper notes particular validity problems when assessors nominated by applicants produce 'inflated, unreliable, and invalid ratings.' Validity checks should consider systematic distortions from assessor selection or conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional criterion: whether peer-review findings and processes generalize across disciplines, applicant pools, and assessor populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors studied thousands of proposals across social science, humanities, and science disciplines and reviewers worldwide; generalizability should be tested across fields and assessor demographics rather than assumed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential biases (applicant, assessor, and interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine potential systematic biases associated with applicants, assessors, and their interactions (examples: age, gender, university, academic rank, research team composition, nationality, experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bias analyses should model applicant effects, assessor effects, and their interactions. The study explicitly evaluated these factors using appropriate multilevel models to detect systematic favoritism or penalty patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant-nominated assessors (conflict of interest risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors nominated by the applicants themselves produced 'inflated, unreliable, and invalid ratings.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat applicant-nominated assessors as high-risk for bias and compromised validity; the authors identify this as the only major systematic bias found and imply policies should limit or carefully manage applicant nomination of reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader system (alternative review approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed new approach to grant review — the reader system — evaluated by the authors with psychology and education grant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reader system was found to be 'substantially more reliable and strategically advantageous' than traditional peer review in their evaluations; consider testing or piloting reader-type systems as a reform to improve reliability and reduce certain biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate statistical models (multilevel cross-classified models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodological standard: evaluate peer-review data using multilevel cross-classified models to partition variance and assess assessor/applicant effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors used multilevel cross-classified models to critically evaluate reviews and detect biases. Use such models (or other suitable hierarchical methods) to account for nested/crossed data structures (applications × assessors) when assessing reliability, validity, and bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility of peer-review findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion concerned with whether peer-review outcomes and research on peer review can be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low reliability undermines reproducibility; peer-review research should report reproducibility indicators and use robust methods to allow replication of bias and reliability findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional competence / assessor experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessors' professional competence, experience, and qualifications (noted among variables such as experience and academic rank) as relevant to review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how assessor experience and competence relate to rating behavior and potential biases; include assessor qualification variables in models to understand their contributions to reliability and validity.
